candidates.name: tenure_cohort
candidates.reason: Non-linear survival hazard (churn drops from 47.4% in year 1 to 6.6% after year 5).
candidates.expected_benefit: Enables linear models to capture non-linear step-function churn drop without high-degree polynomials.
candidates.potential_risk: Redundant with continuous tenure. Tree models may prefer continuous tenure.

candidates.name: total_services
candidates.reason: Measures customer lock-in and product engagement across 8 offerings.
candidates.expected_benefit: Strong monotonic reduction in churn (43.8% at 0 services down to 5.3% at 8 services).
candidates.potential_risk: Correlation with individual service flags (addressed in Phase 6 Feature Selection).

candidates.name: is_auto_pay
candidates.reason: Automatic billing reduces friction and payment defaults (electronic check churn is 45.3% vs ~15% for auto-pay).
candidates.expected_benefit: Clean binary summary of 4 payment methods; separates manual vs automated customers.

candidates.name: has_fiber_optic
candidates.reason: Fiber optic customers churn at 41.89% (highest among all network types) despite generating high revenue.
candidates.expected_benefit: Direct flag for the single most vulnerable infrastructure segment.

candidates.name: has_security_or_techsupport
candidates.reason: OnlineSecurity and TechSupport have the strongest negative association with churn among all add-ons.
candidates.expected_benefit: Subscribers with support churn at 17.07% vs 33.42% for those without.

candidates.name: has_family
candidates.reason: Customers with both a Partner and Dependents experience strong household inertia and shared account stickiness.
candidates.expected_benefit: Churn rate of 14.24% for family accounts vs 30.60% for non-family accounts.
candidates.potential_risk: Low risk; clean orthogonal demographic signal.

candidates.name: is_month_to_month
candidates.reason: Contract type is the single strongest predictor in EDA (Cramer's V = 0.4098).
candidates.expected_benefit: Explicitly separates month-to-month contracts (42.71% churn) from long-term commitments (2-11% churn).

candidates.name: charges_per_tenure
candidates.reason: Hypothesized that ratio of TotalCharges to tenure would capture price trajectory and unexpected billing changes.
candidates.potential_risk: Empirical evaluation showed near-zero target correlation (r = 0.002), extreme skewness, and division-by-zero instability for tenure=0.
candidates.rejection_justification: TotalCharges is mathematically collinear with (tenure * MonthlyCharges). Calculating the ratio produced virtually zero correlation with Churn (r = 0.002) and required artificial epsilon offsets for new customers. Excluded to avoid introducing noise and numerical instability.
